title: Add RAG Authoring Lite: live-edit playground with compact telemetry probes
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add a lightweight RAG authoring playground (devcontainer, live reload, compact telemetry probes) to help teams iterate on prompts, schemas, and indexer config locally.
description:
Summary:
This PR introduces 'RAG Authoring Lite' — a compact, local-first quickstart that gives developers a frictionless authoring loop for retrieval-augmented workflows. It focuses on three core developer needs: (1) immediate live-edit feedback for prompts and structured-output schemas, (2) a tiny local indexer + wasm proxy so authors can iterate without cloud infra, and (3) compact telemetry probes that map to Redwood Console metrics for early visibility.

Motivation & context:
Over the last quarter we've heard repeated feedback from users who need a sandbox that is faster to boot than the full RAG devcontainer and simpler than end-to-end deploys. The goal here is not to replace the full quickstarts but to provide a minimal playground that: boots in < 30s (after first build), supports hot-reload of prompt templates and output validators, and produces a lightweight telemetry summary suitable for embedding into docs and CI smoke checks. This is intended for prototyping and authoring of evals. Linked Linear: ENG-4821 (authoring friction), PM-197 (product quickstart).

What this change includes (high-level):
- new quickstart directory: quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/ with a single-file devcontainer.json and lightweight README.md explaining the workflow.
- a tiny local indexer shim (indexer-lite) implemented as a single Node.js script + optional Go wasm plugin to demonstrate incremental indexing; both run with zero external services.
- a small React playground (static bundle) that watches local files for prompt/schema edits and shows live diffs of generated model output (uses Redwood API JS SDK; example config included).
- compact telemetry probes (probe.yaml) and an adapter that emits local-only metrics compatible with Redwood Console naming (for example: redwood.rag.playground.latency.p50). The adapter prints a JSON summary to stdout for quick CI checks.
- example prompt sets, schema validators (JSON Schema), and a tiny evaluation harness to run deterministic smoke assertions.

Checklist (developer-facing):
- [x] devcontainer + npm start for local preview
- [x] hot reload for prompts and validators
- [x] indexer-lite with incremental add/remove (filesystem-backed)
- [x] telemetry probe adapter and sample probe.yaml
- [x] README with quickstart commands and expected outputs

How to try it locally:
1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite
2) ./devcontainer.json or use Docker: docker compose up --build
3) npm install && npm run start (opens http://localhost:3000)
4) edit prompts/*.md or validators/*.json and see live diffs in the UI; probe summary appears in the server logs.

Security and scope notes:
- The quickstart is explicitly local-only by default: API keys are optional and the indexer stores data in a local ./data folder. The README documents how to wire a hosted Redwood API key if a user wants to test against hosted models.
- No credentials are committed. The devcontainer includes a .devcontainer/README for secret injection.

Commits (summary):
- feat(quickstart): add rag-authoring-lite devcontainer and playground scaffold
- feat(indexer): add indexer-lite (node) + wasm plugin example (go)
- feat(telemetry): add probe.yaml and local adapter + CI smoke script
- docs: add README, quickstart walkthrough, and troubleshooting notes

Changed files (high-level):
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/README.md
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/devcontainer.json
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/package.json, src/ (playground UI)
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/indexer-lite/indexer.js
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/indexer-lite/wasm-plugin/main.go
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/probe.yaml and probes/adapter.js
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/examples/prompts/*.md
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/examples/validators/*.json
- quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/ci/smoke-probes.sh

Review conversation (highlights):
- Jordan Kim: "Nice minimal footprint — can we make the telemetry adapter emit newline-delimited JSON to avoid log parsing edge cases?"
- Maya Patel (author): "Agree, switched adapter to NDJSON output; updated probe.yaml docs and added a lightweight jq example in README."
- Lena Ortiz: "Can the wasm plugin be optional? I worry it adds build friction on Windows."
- Maya Patel: "Yes — wasm plugin is behind a build flag and README documents how to skip it; default devcontainer builds without Go runtime."
- Devon Murphy: "Smoke CI looks good but one flaky test failed once in the e2e job; re-ran pipeline and it passed."

CI details:
- checks: node:install | node:lint | node:test | playground:build | smoke-e2e
- initial run: playground:build failed due to incorrect asset path (fixed in commit 3).
- final status: all checks passed on rerun. CI artifacts include a tiny telemetry summary JSON saved by smoke job.

Testing & validation:
- included unit tests for indexer-lite (adds/removes), playground snapshot for UI, and a smoke script that runs probes against the playground and asserts p50 < 500ms for a synthetic prompt set.

Docs & examples:
- README contains step-by-step authoring scenarios: prompt tuning loop, schema-driven output assertion, probe interpretation, and how to lift to a full quickstart with a remote indexer.
- Example artifacts: two prompt templates (faq and sales), two JSON Schema validators, and a small stepwise eval with expected outputs.

Follow-ups (future work):
- add TypeScript types for the probe adapter and a compact telemetry UI panel inside the playground (ENG-5002).
- upstream an official wasm indexer example if demand grows.

Merge outcome:
Merged via squash on 2026-03-02 after approvals from Jordan Kim and Lena Ortiz. Change is low-risk and gated behind a new quickstarts path; does not alter runtime code.

If you want to try the quickstart quickly: see quickstarts/rag-authoring-lite/README.md for a one-liner that boots the playground in a devcontainer and runs probe smoke checks.
